newsitem.title: INDIA: India says nears Internet service policy.
newsitem.headline: India says nears Internet service policy.

text.p: Two Indian government departments are coordinating efforts to hammer out a policy that would allow the setting up of Internet service providers (ISP), a senior government official said on Monday.
"We are obviously looking at it as a priority area," A.V. Gokak, chairman of the Telecom Commission, told a news conference in New Delhi.

He said the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) and the Department of Electronics (DoE) had completed consultations which would pave the way for a joint paper to be considered by the Telecom Commission as the basis for an Internet policy.
The five-member commission oversees the DoT.
"We should be able to settle the issue at the next meeting of the commission," Gokak said, adding that the date of the next meeting had not yet been scheduled.
State-run Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL) currently has a monopoly on Internet services and a subscriber base of 50,000 connections.

With burgeoning demand anticipated to reach millions of connections, the government has been working to set up a communications infrastructure and a policy that would usher in private Internet service providers.
